item: Airplane mode refuses a request on a keep-alive connection opened before the Stop
summary: R638, from an independent read of R636 (probe_pooled.py, 2026-11-09): the socket guard met a connection only at resolve, connect, tunnel and (R619) an absolute-form request line, so a pooled keep-alive connection opened while the switch was clear kept sending after a Stop; with loopback treated as remote, a requests.Session answered 200, then 200 with the switch engaged, and was refused only on a new connection. src/ingest/airplane.py's putrequest patch now also refuses, while airplane mode is engaged, a request on a connection whose OWN destination is not local: self.host, classified as the connect guard classifies a connect; only an OPEN connection is classified (a fresh one is left to the connect guard, unchanged words); it must have a loopback socket PEER as well as a loopback host name (security read A: urllib3 reports localhost. as localhost); any tunnelling connection (_tunnel_host), urllib3 SOCKS connection (_socks_options, because under TLS the SSLSocket drops PySocks' proxy attribute: both security reads) or PySocks socket with a proxy set counts as not local whatever name it carries; an unreadable host or peer fails closed. Fixed words, never the host (R142). The switch is read where the request is written, so a Stop that lands after a caller's own check is met; the online path costs one flag read and one Event.is_set. activate_kill_switch() now also closes the pooled connections of every EthicalFetcher session and every GuardedSession (a WeakSet under an RLock, registered in their constructors), after the switch is set and never raising; a closed session reopens pools on its next request. Tests (tests/test_airplane_keepalive.py): a connection opened before Stop sends zero further bytes after it; a Stop between the caller's switch read and the send (and inside requests' adapter send) is refused; a tunnelled connection is refused for example.com, localhost and 127.0.0.1; local destinations (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1) still work; requests, urllib.request and http.client end to end; the fetcher's pools empty on Stop and the session works after the switch clears; a removed check lets the request out; urllib3's HTTP/2 connection (which bypasses putrequest) is not injected. R639 (same PR, own commit): while engaged, getaddrinfo is made only for no name, exactly localhost or a loopback literal; a localhost alias (localhost.localdomain, ip6-localhost) that /etc/hosts may not list is refused before any lookup in fixed words, because the resolver otherwise asked DNS (security read A); plain names keep the sentence the offline readers parse; and exactly localhost is answered from 127.0.0.1 / ::1 (IPv4 first) instead of a libc name lookup, because a hosts file without an entry for the family asked for sent it to DNS (read A, strace); socket.connect/connect_ex/create_connection handed a host name apply the same rule before the real call (an alias refused, localhost swapped for the socket family's literal), because CPython resolves a connect name through libc, not the patched getaddrinfo (S1's read: strace showed connect to localhost.localdomain query DNS); tests use the spy resolver, no real DNS. docs/SECURITY.md states the residual against the 16-library socket-importer allowlist (imaplib/poplib mailbox pull already connected finishes its pull, to be closed by R640; httpx loopback LLM clients; native code) and why patching socket send (option b) was declined. Stated residuals, ruled R641 for a later PR: gethostbyname/gethostbyname_ex unpatched, UDP sendto/sendmsg to a remote address not refused. Release-notes line: with airplane mode on, a web connection the app opened before you went offline can no longer be used to send a request, the app's collection sessions close their idle connections the moment you go offline, and the app no longer asks DNS to look up localhost or a localhost alias while offline.
